title: What the prostate contributes to reproduction and urination
intro: The prostate is a gland below the bladder, surrounding part of the urethra. It contributes fluid to semen rather than producing sperm cells. Its position explains why enlargement can affect urine flow, but not every urinary symptom is caused by it.

sections.heading: Making fluid
paragraphs: Prostate secretions mix with sperm from the testes and fluid from other glands. Muscle contractions help move semen into the urethra during ejaculation.

sections.heading: Different pathways
paragraphs: Urine and semen use the urethra at different times with coordinated closure and muscle action. Ejaculation, erection and bladder emptying are related but distinct functions.

sections.heading: Growth and symptoms
paragraphs: Age-related enlargement may narrow the urine passage and cause weak flow or incomplete emptying. Size alone does not determine severity, and benign enlargement is not the same diagnosis as cancer.

sections.heading: Assessment
paragraphs: Discuss symptoms, medicines and preferences. Examination, urine tests and selected further tests help clarify causes. A prostate-specific antigen result needs interpretation; it does not by itself prove or exclude cancer.

sections.heading: Seeking help
paragraphs: New blood in urine needs assessment. Inability to pass urine, especially with pain, or urinary symptoms with fever and severe illness needs urgent care. Do not try to solve acute retention by simply drinking much more.

A diagram explains typical structure, not the cause of an individual symptom. Before a consultation, note when a change began, what brings it on and how it affects daily activities. Bring previous results and ask how the findings fit together.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira helps a relative list urinary symptoms and medicines before a visit rather than assuming all night-time urination is the prostate.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben cannot pass urine despite a painful full bladder. He seeks urgent help instead of waiting for a supplement to shrink the gland.
